item.title: Research Assistant
item.description:
Build a persistent research assistant that ingests academic papers, extracts structured facts into the memory graph, and answers cross-session questions with citations.

Overview

A Friday agent configured for deep research with long-term memory of sources, topics explored, and findings. The agent maintains context across weeks of research sessions, tracks which papers have been read, remembers insights from previous explorations, and builds a knowledge graph of research topics.

Key Capabilities:

  • Web search and document ingestion
  • Citation tracking and source management
  • Topic clustering and relationship mapping
  • Cross-session research continuity
  • Automatic insight extraction and summarization

name: researcher
role: "Research Assistant"
goal: "Conduct thorough research, track sources, and build comprehensive knowledge over time"

system_prompt: |
  You are a research assistant specializing in {{domain}}.

  Your task is to find accurate, relevant information and build a comprehensive
  knowledge base across multiple research sessions.

  Core Responsibilities:
  - Search for and analyze information from multiple sources
  - Always cite sources with URLs when available
  - Track which papers/articles you've already reviewed
  - Distinguish between facts, expert opinions, and speculation
  - Acknowledge uncertainty when information is incomplete or conflicting
  - Build connections between related research topics
  - Summarize findings in clear, structured formats
  - Remember prior research to avoid duplication

  Current research focus: {{focus}}

  When you encounter a topic you've researched before, reference your prior findings
  and explain what's new or different in the current exploration.

tools:
  - web_search
  - scrape_page
  - read_file
  - write_file
  - http_request
  - parse_json

tool_autonomy: auto

model: "gpt-4o"
temperature: 0.3   # Lower temperature for factual accuracy
max_tokens: 4096

memory_config:
  mode: full
  enable_graph: true    # Graph tracks: Papers, Authors, Topics, Concepts
  enable_vector: true   # Vector stores: Insights, summaries, source excerpts
  max_episodic_turns: 50

  priming:
    enabled: true
    top_entities: 30   # Load many entities (papers, topics)
    max_insights: 40   # Rich prior research context
    recency_days: 90   # 3 months of research history

  lifecycle:
    decay_rate: 0.005  # Slow decay — research stays relevant
    promotion_threshold: 0.65

item.title: Code Development Assistant
item.description:
A multi-agent pipeline where a coordinator delegates code review, test generation, and refactoring to specialist agents that share a common memory of the codebase.

Overview

A Friday multi-agent system for software development featuring three specialized agents: a coder, a reviewer, and a tester. Agents share memory of codebase context, prior reviews, and coding patterns, enabling consistent code quality and continuous learning from feedback.

Key Capabilities:

  • Code generation with style consistency
  • Automated code review (style, bugs, security)
  • Test generation and execution
  • Memory of coding patterns and preferences
  • Multi-agent peer review with human approval gates

id: implement_feature
name: "Feature Implementation"
description: "Multi-agent workflow: Code -> Review -> Test -> Commit"
version: "1.0.0"

tasks:
  - id: code_feature
    name: "Implement Feature"
    description: |
      Implement: {{feature_description}}
      Save to the appropriate file.
    agent: coder
    inputs:
      feature_description: "$user_feature"
      target_file: "$user_file"
    outputs:
      - implementation_code
      - file_path
    requires_approval: false

  - id: review_code
    name: "Code Review"
    description: |
      Review code for correctness, security, style, and documentation.
      Provide feedback with severity levels.
    agent: reviewer
    inputs:
      code: "$implementation_code"
      file_path: "$file_path"
    outputs:
      - review_feedback
      - approval_status
    depends_on:
      - code_feature
    requires_approval: false

  - id: approval_gate
    name: "Human Review Gate"
    description: "Review code and reviewer feedback before proceeding."
    agent: reviewer
    inputs:
      code: "$implementation_code"
      feedback: "$review_feedback"
    outputs:
      - approved_code
    depends_on:
      - review_code
    requires_approval: true   # Human gate

  - id: generate_tests
    name: "Generate Test Suite"
    description: |
      Generate unit tests, edge case tests, and error handling tests.
      Use pytest framework with clear test names.
    agent: tester
    inputs:
      code: "$approved_code"
      file_path: "$file_path"
    outputs:
      - test_code
      - test_file_path
    depends_on:
      - approval_gate
    requires_approval: false

  - id: run_tests
    name: "Execute Test Suite"
    description: |
      Run generated tests and report results.
      Include pass/fail counts, coverage, and failure details.
    agent: tester
    inputs:
      test_file: "$test_file_path"
    outputs:
      - test_results
      - coverage_report
    depends_on:
      - generate_tests
    requires_approval: false

  - id: commit_changes
    name: "Git Commit"
    description: |
      Commit the implementation and tests following Conventional Commits:
      feat(module): Brief description
    agent: coder
    inputs:
      code_file: "$file_path"
      test_file: "$test_file_path"
      results: "$test_results"
      review: "$review_feedback"
    outputs:
      - commit_sha
    depends_on:
      - run_tests
    requires_approval: true   # Human approves commit

Ingest large enterprise document corpora into Friday’s vector store and enable natural language Q&A with provenance citations back to the source document and page.

Overview

Friday can serve as a knowledge management layer over large enterprise document sets — policy manuals, technical specifications, legal contracts, or knowledge base articles. Documents are chunked, embedded, and stored in the vector store. When users ask questions, Friday retrieves the most relevant chunks and synthesizes a grounded answer with citations.

Key Capabilities:

  • Batch document ingestion (PDF, DOCX, HTML, Markdown)
  • Semantic search across all ingested documents
  • Answer synthesis with source citations and confidence scores
  • Follow-up question support with conversational context
  • Multi-collection organization (by department, date, document type)

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path
from friday_memory import MemoryController
from friday_tools import file_read

async def ingest_document_corpus(
    documents_path: str,
    collection_name: str = "enterprise_docs",
    chunk_size: int = 500,
    chunk_overlap: int = 50,
):
    """
    Ingest a corpus of documents into Friday's vector store.

    Args:
        documents_path: Directory containing documents to ingest
        collection_name: ChromaDB collection to store documents in
        chunk_size: Token size of each chunk
        chunk_overlap: Overlap between consecutive chunks
    """
    memory = MemoryController.from_config("config.yaml")

    docs_dir = Path(documents_path)
    supported_extensions = {".pdf", ".docx", ".txt", ".md", ".html"}

    total_chunks = 0

    for doc_path in docs_dir.rglob("*"):
        if doc_path.suffix.lower() not in supported_extensions:
            continue

        print(f"Ingesting: {doc_path.name}")

        # Read document
        content = await file_read(str(doc_path))

        # Chunk document
        chunks = chunk_text(content, chunk_size=chunk_size, overlap=chunk_overlap)

        # Store each chunk with metadata
        for i, chunk in enumerate(chunks):
            await memory.vector_store.add_document(
                content=chunk,
                metadata={
                    "source": doc_path.name,
                    "source_path": str(doc_path),
                    "chunk_index": i,
                    "total_chunks": len(chunks),
                    "doc_type": doc_path.suffix[1:],
                },
                collection=collection_name,
            )

        total_chunks += len(chunks)
        print(f"  -> {len(chunks)} chunks stored")

    print(f"\nIngestion complete: {total_chunks} total chunks stored")


def chunk_text(text: str, chunk_size: int = 500, overlap: int = 50) -> list[str]:
    """Split text into overlapping chunks by word count."""
    words = text.split()
    chunks = []

    i = 0
    while i < len(words):
        chunk = " ".join(words[i : i + chunk_size])
        chunks.append(chunk)
        i += chunk_size - overlap

    return chunks


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(ingest_document_corpus(
        documents_path="./enterprise_docs/",
        collection_name="enterprise_knowledge_base",
    ))

  document library. Your role is to answer questions accurately and
  always cite your sources.

  Guidelines:
  - Always cite the source document and relevant excerpt
  - If information is not in the knowledge base, say so clearly
  - Do not speculate beyond what the documents state
  - When multiple documents are relevant, synthesize a comprehensive answer
  - Note when information may be outdated

  Citation format:
  [Source: {document_name}, Section: {section}]

model: "gpt-4o"
temperature: 0.1   # Low temperature for factual accuracy

memory_config:
  mode: full
  enable_vector: true   # Primary retrieval from document corpus
  enable_graph: false   # Not needed for document QA
  enable_episodic: true # Track conversation for follow-up questions

  retrieval:
    collection: "enterprise_knowledge_base"
    top_k: 10           # Retrieve more chunks for comprehensive answers
    min_similarity: 0.65

User: "What is our vacation policy for part-time employees?"

Friday: Based on the employee handbook:

Part-time employees working more than 20 hours per week accrue vacation
at a rate of 0.5 days per month (6 days annually). Employees working

Vacation may be carried over up to a maximum of 5 days into the following
calendar year. Any unused vacation beyond this limit is forfeited.

[Source: HR_Policy_Update_Q3_2025.docx, Section: Part-Time Benefits Amendment]

Note: The HR Policy Update from Q3 2025 amended Section 4.2 of the handbook.
The amendment supersedes the original handbook text where they conflict.

---

User: "What about sick leave?"

Friday: Continuing from the same policy documents:

Both full-time and part-time employees (working 20+ hours/week) accrue
1 day of sick leave per month, up to a maximum of 10 days annually.
Sick leave does not carry over between calendar years.

Employees must notify their manager before the start of their shift when
taking sick leave. Medical documentation is required for absences exceeding
3 consecutive business days.

item.title: Compliance-Ready Deployment
item.description:
Deploy Friday in compliance-sensitive environments using local LLMs, encrypted storage, structured audit logging, and data-residency controls aligned with HIPAA, GDPR, and SOC 2.

Compliance Requirements by Framework

HIPAA (Healthcare)

Protected Health Information (PHI) cannot leave approved infrastructure without a Business Associate Agreement (BAA). OpenAI and Anthropic offer BAAs for enterprise customers, but most providers do not.

Friday’s HIPAA-Aligned Architecture:

  • Local LLMs (Ollama with Llama 3 or Mistral) — zero data egress
  • Encrypted SQLite for transcript storage (AES-256 via LUKS)
  • Encrypted ChromaDB persist directory
  • Audit trail via transcript.recording.record_tools: true
  • No web tool access to external endpoints

GDPR (EU Data Residency)

GDPR requires that EU personal data is processed only on EU infrastructure, and gives individuals the right to erasure.

Friday’s GDPR-Aligned Architecture:

  • Self-hosted deployment on EU cloud region or on-premises
  • Right to erasure: delete user’s session data from all three stores (vector, graph, episodic)
  • Data minimization: configure extraction to avoid storing unnecessary personal details
  • Consent audit trail: log all memory write operations

SOC 2 (Enterprise SaaS)

SOC 2 requires audit trails for all data access and encryption in transit and at rest.

Friday’s SOC 2-Aligned Architecture:

  • TLS for all network communication
  • Encryption at rest for all data stores
  • Structured JSON audit logs via the tool audit system
  • Access control policies via tool allowlists
  • Session and user attribution in all transcript records

For the strictest compliance requirements, use a fully air-gapped configuration that makes no external API calls.

from cryptography.fernet import Fernet
from friday_transcript import TranscriptStore

class EncryptedTranscriptStore(TranscriptStore):
    """TranscriptStore wrapper that encrypts all message content."""

    def __init__(self, encryption_key: bytes, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.cipher = Fernet(encryption_key)

    async def store_turn(self, turn):
        """Encrypt messages before writing to storage."""
        turn.user_message = self.cipher.encrypt(
            turn.user_message.encode()
        ).decode()
        turn.assistant_message = self.cipher.encrypt(
            turn.assistant_message.encode()
        ).decode()
        await super().store_turn(turn)

    async def get_turn(self, turn_id: str):
        """Decrypt messages after reading from storage."""
        turn = await super().get_turn(turn_id)
        turn.user_message = self.cipher.decrypt(
            turn.user_message.encode()
        ).decode()
        turn.assistant_message = self.cipher.decrypt(
            turn.assistant_message.encode()
        ).decode()
        return turn

async def erase_user_data(user_id: str, memory_controller):
    """
    Erase all stored data for a user (GDPR Article 17).

    Removes from: vector store, graph store, episodic store.
    """
    logger.info(f"Starting data erasure for user: {user_id}")

    # 1. Erase from vector store (all collections)
    collections = ["short_term", "long_term", "decayed"]
    for collection in collections:
        deleted = await memory_controller.vector_store.delete_by_filter(
            filters={"user_id": user_id},
            collection=collection,
        )
        logger.info(f"Vector store ({collection}): deleted {deleted} documents")

    # 2. Erase from graph store
    entities = await memory_controller.graph_store.get_entities_by_user(user_id)
    for entity in entities:
        await memory_controller.graph_store.remove_entity(entity.name)
    logger.info(f"Graph store: deleted {len(entities)} entities")

    # 3. Erase from episodic store (transcripts)
    sessions = await memory_controller.episodic_store.get_sessions_by_user(user_id)
    for session in sessions:
        await memory_controller.episodic_store.delete_session(session.id)
    logger.info(f"Episodic store: deleted {len(sessions)} sessions")

    logger.info(f"Data erasure complete for user: {user_id}")
    return {
        "user_id": user_id,
        "status": "erased",
        "timestamp": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
    }

tools:
  security:
    filesystem:
      allowed_paths:
        - "/workspace"
        - "/data/friday"
      blocked_paths:
        - "/etc"
        - "/root"
        - "/var/log"    # Prevent log tampering
        - "/proc"
        - "/sys"
      max_file_size_mb: 10

    shell:
      allowed_commands:
        - "ls"
        - "cat"
        - "grep"
      blocked_commands:
        - "rm -rf"
        - "dd"
        - "chmod 777"
        - "curl"
        - "wget"
      blocked_patterns:
        - ".*sudo.*"
        - ".*curl.*\\|.*bash.*"

    network:
      enabled: false    # Complete network isolation

Compliance Checklist

Before going live in a regulated environment:

  • All LLM calls route to approved infrastructure (local or BAA-covered cloud)
  • Encryption at rest enabled for all data directories
  • TLS enabled for all inter-service communication
  • Audit logging enabled with structured JSON output
  • Sensitive data patterns configured for redaction in logs
  • Tool network access disabled or allowlisted to approved domains
  • Right-to-erasure procedure documented and tested
  • Access control policies applied (tool allowlists)
  • Backup and retention policies defined
  • Incident response procedure documented
